properties.description:
User need from the MVP readiness audit: the user must explicitly control acknowledgement of changes. Opening, reading, selecting or otherwise viewing an item must not automatically conclude that its changes are known or no longer need attention; implicit transitions can cause missed work.

The user proposes three distinct attention meanings: changes still need acknowledgement; changes are acknowledged but processing is deliberately deferred; the item needs no attention until further changes occur. Choose short UI labels later, not the user's long descriptive phrases. Acknowledgement and processing are distinct. Preserve attention across task moves between Queued, Running and Blocked and consider completed-work history as well; attention should not be inferred from lifecycle placement.

Design implications to validate: new changes must remain apparent even when an earlier version was acknowledged, and a concurrent new change must not be silently cleared by acknowledgement of an older one. Team scope, own edits, change granularity and which routine agent events count are not fully specified. Do not turn these open details into an automatic-read acknowledgement heuristic. No UI layout or storage schema has been selected.
properties.title: Explicit acknowledgement of changes across activity states
